findings.claim: CARRIED FORWARD (NO ACTION). _resolve_audit_key_id except clause covers (ValueError, OSError, AttributeError) but omits IndexError. Path.parents[2] in project_root() raises IndexError if the resolved install path has fewer than 3 components. The 'NEVER blocks a tool call' invariant is not formally unconditional across all exception types.
findings.evidence: tools.py line 443: 'except (ValueError, OSError, AttributeError): return "key-ring-unreadable"'. project_root() returns Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]; .parents[2] raises IndexError for paths with < 3 components. R1 FIX-ROUND-1.md explicitly marks MIN-SAFE-001 'NO ACTION': 'Defensive broadening is a tradeoff; current scope matches what _current_signing_key_id actually raises.' No change introduced by fix-round-1. New tests test_log_attribution_falls_back_when_key_ring_empty and test_log_attribution_falls_back_when_key_ring_missing exercise ValueError and OSError paths only; IndexError path remains untested by the test suite.
findings.impact: Functionally impossible in any realistic pip/uv deployment where __file__ resolves to a path with ≥ 3 components. The forward-looking risk is that a future project_root() refactor introducing RuntimeError or IndexError would silently break the fallback guarantee without a failing test catching it. Severity unchanged at MIN.
findings.mitigation: Widen to 'except Exception' with a TOOL_LOGGER.warning("_resolve_audit_key_id fallback triggered: %s", repr(exc)) observability line. One-line change. Acceptable to carry forward per R1 disposition; does not block APPROVED_WITH_FINDINGS verdict.

findings.claim: CARRIED FORWARD (operational-gate tracking). Audit attribution is fully degraded in current operational state: docs/security/mcp-signing-keys.pub contains only comments, so every tool invocation logs key_id=key-ring-unreadable. USER-GATE-D criterion (vi) now explicitly requires BOTH code AND operational satisfaction before the operator can check the box.
findings.evidence: docs/gates/USER-GATE-D.md criterion (vi): 'Both code AND operational must be satisfied to check this box. … docs/security/mcp-signing-keys.pub actually contains an active key entry. Currently empty (comment-only) — until the operator generates + commits a key, audit attribution falls back to the key-ring-unreadable sentinel.' The pub file was not modified in fix-round-1 (FIX-ROUND-1.md inline-fix list items 1–7 do not include mcp-signing-keys.pub). Every MCP tool call in the current deployment logs key_id=key-ring-unreadable.
findings.impact: Until the operator runs keygen and commits the public key, audit logs cannot attribute tool invocations to a key identity. propose() also remains blocked (raises SCP-MCP-E021 on an empty/unsigned ring). Impact is bounded: the degradation is acknowledged, tracked, and gated by USER-GATE-D criterion (vi) which cannot be checked without resolving it. No active exploit path exists because (a) single-operator mode means no second maintainer can act on the degraded log, and (b) the gate blocks false Threshold A closure.
findings.mitigation: Operator must generate and commit a key to docs/security/mcp-signing-keys.pub before checking USER-GATE-D criterion (vi). No code change required. The tightened criterion (vi) language now explicitly enforces this as an operational pre-condition. Carry forward.
